September 29, 2026

James Chessell’s move from the AFR to Joe Aston’s Rampart is another sign of a media landscape being remade. Smaller outlets, subscription models, podcasts, and independent publishers are challenging the power once held by newspapers, radio and television.

The surprise move by the editor-in-chief of the Australian Financial Review, James Chessell, to Joe Aston’s online media start-up Rampart highlights the structural changes at play in the media industry.

On one level, Chessell is leaving a top job at the Nine media group to join his friend and former AFR columnist for a bold new venture which has already notched up a solid track record after only 18 months.

Before the start of training camp on Tuesday, the Nuggets indulged local reporters for a couple of hours on the practice court at Ball Arena on Monday afternoon. Here are five things we learned from the team’s annual preseason media day.

Nuggets lead executives Jon Wallace and Ben Tenzer commented for the first time on their controversial decision to trade restricted free agent Peyton Watson this offseason, enabling him to join the Cleveland Cavaliers on a four-year, $88 million contract.

“Peyton did a lot of great things here. Great person. Great player,” Tenzer said. “It was amazing to watch this growth, especially last season when he took a big jump.
